thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: High-volume routing fallback oscillation detected for service=redwood-inference (text-gen). Regions involved: us-east <-> us-west <-> eu-west. Alert spike 58/min, error-class=health-flap. Created thread for triage.

maya (oncall): I'm on it. Seeing healthcheck failures from us-east -> traffic routes to us-west -> then eu-west picks up -> back to us-east. It's repeating ~2m cycles. Customer complaints coming in about intermittent 502s and increased tail latency.

sanjeev (infra): digging into probe aggregator logs. Early hypothesis: probe responses occasionally mark nodes UNHEALTHY for a single sample and routing immediately fails over. Looks like a windowing bug in the aggregator TTL logic. Pasting the condensed log:```
2026-03-15T14:11:05Z probe(us-east-1a) status=OK ttl=5s seq=10234
2026-03-15T14:11:06Z probe(us-east-1a) status=FAIL ttl=0s seq=10235 reason="stale-detect"
2026-03-15T14:11:07Z probe(us-west-2b) status=OK ttl=5s seq=10236
2026-03-15T14:11:08Z probe(eu-west-1c) status=OK ttl=5s seq=10237
2026-03-15T14:11:09Z probe(us-east-1a) status=OK ttl=5s seq=10238
```
Notice the single FAIL in us-east and immediate routing decision.

maya (oncall): Confirmed in dashboards — health state flips to DEGRADED -> UNHEALTHY in 1 sample, routing policy fallback triggers immediately. That causes cross-region traffic which increases latency then some regions hop back. Patient customers see spikes.

kevin (product): Quick customer impact summary please. Which tenants? SLA exposure?

ops-anna: From telemetry over the last 10m: ~12,300 requests impacted, error rate bump to 2.1% (502s/timeouts) for the affected frontends. Top impacted customers: two mid-market tenants with heavy burst traffic (ids redacted), no enterprise SLAs breached yet but margin close. Estimated 3.5 hours of elevated error rate if we don't mitigate.

maya (oncall): Immediate mitigation plan: 1) Temporarily disable cross-region fallback for text-gen route (prefer local region + queue/buffer instead) 2) Increase probe aggregator hysteresis (require 2 consecutive fails before marking unhealthy) 3) Patch probe aggregator dedupe ordering and roll to canary.

sanjeev (infra): Applying mitigation 1 now. Command run:```
$ redwoodctl routing set-policy --service text-gen --region us-east --fallback disabled --reason "temp-mitigation health-flap 2332109876"
Applied policy to us-east: fallback=disabled
$ redwoodctl routing snapshot --service text-gen --since 5m
[us-east] state=PRIMARY fallback=disabled
[us-west] state=SECONDARY fallback=disabled
[eu-west] state=SECONDARY fallback=disabled
```
Result: traffic should stop cross-region bouncing; local nodes will queue up to burst capacity.

maya (oncall): Observing metrics: within 60s, cross-region route count down ~85%, tail latency in affected customers down ~300ms, error-rate trending down. Marking mitigation as effective for now.

tara (sre): I'll take the handoff for live watch and do the patch rollout. Oncoming: tara — will monitor for 60m and run canary deploy of fix to probe aggregator (eu-west first).

sanjeev (infra): Root cause update: probe-aggregator uses a circular buffer keyed by (node, region) but when probe latency > heartbeatTTL, entries can be reordered so a single stale negative sample is interpreted as current. Patch: require consecutive fails within window and use monotonic timestamps for ordering. Quick patch below:```diff
- if (sample.timestamp < latest_ts) mark_stale();
+ if (sample.timestamp <= latest_ts) continue; // drop out-of-order
+ if (consecutive_failures[node] >= 2) mark_unhealthy(node);
```
I'll push to canary and monitor.

ops-anna: Noted. Customer comms draft: "We've mitigated a routing oscillation affecting requests to text-gen by temporarily restricting cross-region failover while we deploy a fix. Customers may have seen short-lived 5xx errors; service is being monitored and we'll follow up with postmortem." Send after we confirm stable for 30m.

kevin (product): cc @sales @legal on impacted accounts. Add note to customer status page and start an incident banner.

maya (oncall): Canary deploy to eu-west started. Running health checks and sampling http responses.

sanjeev (infra): Canary looks good after 2 cycles. Rolling patch to us-west now, then us-east. Commands:```
$ deployctl rollout probe-aggregator v1.2.3-canary --region eu-west --wait
canary ok -> promoting to us-west
deploy ok -> promoting to us-east
```

tara (sre): After rollout, we observe aggregator no longer marks single-sample fails as UNHEALTHY. Charts show stable health flags and no new cross-region handoffs in the last 8m.

maya (oncall): Preparing rollback plan to re-enable fallback: will re-enable fallback after 30m of stable metrics and a 15m green window. Re-enable command will be communicated.

incident-bot: routing policy changed by sanjeev at 2332110200 (policy=fallback disabled for text-gen in us-east/us-west/eu-west).

sanjeev (infra): Root cause summary for postmortem: probe-aggregator timestamp ordering + strict 1-sample fail threshold -> transient GC/net jitter caused single-sample marking -> immediate fallback policy executed -> created three-way oscillation. Fix: add ordering guard and 2-sample hysteresis; default policy to require 2 consecutive fails.

maya (oncall): Customer impact note: 12.3k affected requests, peak error-rate 2.1%, duration ~45 minutes from first alert to stable green in our mitigation window. No paid-SLA breaches detected but escalation to sales/AE recommended for affected tenants.

kevin (product): Postmortem owners: sanjeev (root cause + infra fix), tara (deployment + monitoring), maya (ops timeline + customer comms). Target initial postmortem doc by EOD and full RCA in 48h.

ops-anna: I'll prepare status update and draft customer message. Will include suggested compensation if any customers request it.

maya (oncall): Handoff to tara for active monitoring. I'm signing off from live tab. If anything flips back, page me.

tara (sre): Taking watch. Setting an alert to auto-escalate if health flips >2 times in 10m.

kevin (product): Thx team. Follow up: review default routing thresholds in design doc and propose safer defaults (2-sample hysteresis). Also consider lighting a circuit-breaker instead of immediate cross-region failover next quarter.

incident-bot: Thread closed for active triage handoff at 2332110500.

maya (oncall): Recording action items:
- sanjeev: ship patch to probe-aggregator (done) + update canary notes (due now)
- tara: maintain watch for 60m, then clear alerting plan (in progress)
- maya: publish incident summary + trigger postmortem doc (EOD)
- ops-anna: draft customer communication and incident banner (in progress)
- kevin: coordinate sales/legal outreach for impacted accounts

End of thread.
